summary: S. Krishnaswami Aiyangar studied at the University of Madras (~1893–1899). Working in Indology and history and archaeology, he held the Chair of Indian History and Archæology at the University of Madras (~1914–1929).

An Indologist and philosopher, S. Kuppuswami Sastri served at Presidency College, Chennai, and the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library (~1914–1935). He was later Honorary Professor and Dean at Annamalai University (~1935–1943) and Professor at Presidency University, Kolkata.

S. N. Balagangadhara studied at Ghent University. Working in philosophy and religious studies, he served at Ghent University (~1991–2018) as Professor in Comparative Science of Cultures and Director of the Research Centre Vergelijkende Cultuurwetenschap.
S. N. Savadi worked in Indology and held posts at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, attested in 1953 and 1969.

Working in philosophy and Indology, S. S. Suryanarayana Sastri was Reader in Indian Philosophy (attested 1929) and later Reader and Head of the Department of Philosophy (attested 1942) at the University of Madras.

S. Sankaranarayanan worked in Indology, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He was an Honorary Professor at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (~1985–1999) and held a post at the Chinmaya International Foundation in 1999.

Sabine Löhr studied Indology at the University of Freiburg and the University of Hamburg (M.A.), where she completed doctoral studies under Lambert Schmithausen. She also served as a Wissenschaftliche Hilfskraft at the University of Hamburg.

Working in Buddhist studies, Sadahiko Kariya served as an assistant professor at Shuchiin University (attested 1977) and as a professor in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies at Chizan Senmon Gakko (attested 2001).
Sadajiro Sugiura studied at Rikkyo University and earned a PhD from the University of Pennsylvania (~1898–1900). Working in philosophy and Buddhist studies, he later held a post at Rikkyo University.
Saileswar Sen worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Calcutta until 1920 and completed his doctoral studies under Barend Faddegon.
Sakda Hemthep worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies, earning an MPhil from Cardiff University in 2014 under the supervision of Max Deeg.
Sakya Trizin studied Tibetology and Buddhist studies under teachers including Khenpo Appey, Tritsho Khenpo Rinchen, and the 14th Dalai Lama, Tenzin Gyatso.
Working in Buddhist and religious studies, Sakyong Mipham studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Khenpo Namdrol, Penor Rinpoche, and Chögyam Trungpa, whom he later succeeded.

Sallie B. King studied at the University of British Columbia and under Leon Hurvitz (~1975–1981). Working in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies, she was Professor of Philosophy and Religion at James Madison University (~1991–2017).

Sally J. Sutherland Goldman earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley (1979), studying under Shivaram Dattatray Joshi and T. Shrinivas Shastri. She held a post at UC Berkeley (attested 1996) in Indology and linguistics.
Sally McAra worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies, earning an MA from the University of Auckland (1999–2000) under the supervision of Christine Dureau and Karen Nero.
Sally Mellick Cutler earned a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford in 1993. Working in Buddhist studies and Indology, she served as manager of the Pali Text Society Office (attested 1997).

Salomon Lefmann studied Indology and linguistics at the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1858–1864) under Franz Bopp. He later held the Extraordinariat für Sanskrit at Heidelberg University (~1866–1912).
Sam Harris studied philosophy at Stanford University (~1986–2000), studied at UCLA in 2009, and was taught by Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche (~1988–1996) and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje (~1989–1999).

Sam van Schaik studied at the University of Manchester (~1999–2004) and under Lama Jampa Thaye, Karma Thinley Rinpoche, and Sakya Trizin. In Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he held posts at the British Library (~2003–2017).
